sources.entry: LocationSimulator - Application to spoof your iOS or iPhoneSimulator location.

summary.one_liner: LocationSimulator is a macOS app that spoofs the GPS location of iOS, iPadOS, and tvOS devices and the iPhoneSimulator, aimed at developers testing location-based apps.
summary.what_it_does: The app lets you set a device's reported location by long-clicking a point on a map, without jailbreaking the device or installing anything on it. It supports walk, cycle and drive movement presets as well as custom speeds, and you can steer movement with the arrow keys or drag a direction indicator. It can also navigate from the current location to a new point, and it includes location search. Devices can be connected over USB or, after configuring Finder sync, over Wi-Fi. The app tries to download the DeveloperDiskImage files for the device's iOS version from GitHub, and the README describes a manual copy path if that fails. The README also mentions GPX parsing and a help book as part of the project's internal packages.
use_cases: Test location-based features of an iOS app
Simulate movement along a route for app testing
Set a device location over Wi-Fi without USB
Test an app's behavior in different cities or countries
how_to_run: Install Homebrew (see the README for the install command)
Connect the iOS device via USB or Wi-Fi and select it in the sidebar
Long-click the map to set the current location
Use the walk button, arrow keys, or navigation prompt to move; click the reset button to stop spoofing
notable: Spoofs location on iOS devices without a jailbreak or on-device app
Supports the iPhoneSimulator as well as physical devices
Built as a standalone app that no longer needs Xcode at runtime
Movement control via arrow keys, auto-move, and custom speeds
Wi-Fi device support via Finder network sync
caveats: The README states that iOS 17 and later are not supported by the source code in this repo
Building from source requires Xcode, Jekyll, and several companion Swift packages
Some iOS versions need DeveloperDiskImage files that the author cannot distribute; manual setup may be needed
The README says the author maintains the project in spare time, and a closed-source successor (LocationSimulator2) is in beta
